questiontext.text:
Goal

A miller receives water-level changes as text, including rises and falls. Total the changes, stopping if a reading cannot be converted.

Read
  • Errors are values. Find the block with three calls to fd.Write. What does the code do immediately after each call that can fail?
  • Errors in the spec. Read the sentence after the interface. Which error value means that no error occurred?
  • strconv.Atoi. Its documentation names the function that it uses. In that function's error paragraph, what number accompanies an out-of-range error?
Coming from Java

The reflex is Integer.parseInt inside a try, with a NumberFormatException caught somewhere above. The Go conversion throws nothing, so there is nothing to catch.

try {
    total += Integer.parseInt(reading);
} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
    throw new IllegalArgumentException("smudged reading", e);
}
Banned: panic
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Find the GoCon story in the blog. Use the check after each fd.Write once inside your loop.
  • For readings that all convert, check the value returned beside the sum. Compare it with the specification sentence.

testcode.text: var n int _, err := total([]string{"7", "smudge", "2", "torn"}) fmt.Println(err) n, err = total([]string{"1", "99999999999999999999"}) fmt.Println(n, err)

expected.text: strconv.Atoi: parsing "smudge": invalid syntax 0 strconv.Atoi: parsing "99999999999999999999": value out of range

testcode.text: n, err := total(nil) fmt.Println(n, err == nil) n, err = total([]string{"-4", "9", "0"}) fmt.Println(n, err == nil) _, err = total([]string{"4", ""}) fmt.Println(err)

expected.text: 0 true 5 true strconv.Atoi: parsing "": invalid syntax

questiontext.text:
Goal

A parcel counter rejects unsuitable parcels before printing their labels. Complete its checks without nesting them.

Read
  • errors. Read the second overview sentence and open the named function in the index. Where does the returned error get its text?
Coming from Java

The reflex is an if, else if, else sequence ending in a throw, or nested if blocks with the success branch innermost. Neither shape passes the rules below.

if (p.weight() < 1) {
    throw new IllegalArgumentException("empty parcel");
} else if (p.weight() > 20000) {
    throw new IllegalArgumentException("too heavy");
} else {
    return p.dest() + " " + p.weight() + "g";
}
Banned: else
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If a parcel that breaks two rules reports the wrong error, compare the order of your checks with the order beside label.
  • If a parcel that passes every check reports an error, look at what you return beside the label.

testcode.text: s, err := label(Parcel{Weight: 1200, Dest: "Leeds"}) fmt.Println(s, err == nil)
_, err := label(Parcel{Weight: 0, Dest: "Leeds"}) fmt.Println(err) _, err = label(Parcel{Weight: 800}) fmt.Println(err)
_, err := label(Parcel{}) fmt.Println(err) _, err = label(Parcel{Weight: 25000}) fmt.Println(err)

questiontext.text:
Goal

A keep's sentinel records refusals, and clerks add notes as the log travels. Help the captain recognise the original reason through those notes.

Read
  • errors.Is. Read the first sentence and the paragraph that defines the error tree. Besides err itself, what can err's tree contain?
  • errors.New. Read the second sentence. If two calls use identical text, how many distinct error values do they create?
  • io, the Variables section. Inspect EOF and the nearby variables. Are these values created once or once per call? Ignore the note about the equality operator because the red line bans that operator.
Coming from Java

The reflex is one exception class per refusal with a catch block for each, or a comparison on getMessage(). A hidden test punishes both.

try {
    gate.admit(name, hour);
} catch (NotInvitedException e) {
    return "turned away, fetch the steward";
} catch (CurfewException e) {
    return "turned away, come back at dawn";
}
Banned: ==. Required: errors.Is
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • If an error with a note gets the plain turned away, reread errors.Is on what err's tree holds beyond err itself.
  • If Admit's error does not match ErrNotInvited, count the calls to errors.New in your file against that function's second sentence.

expected.text: admitted turned away, fetch the steward
admitted turned away, wait by the fire turned away, come back at dawn

testcode.text: g := NewGate([]string{"Ada"}, 22, 3) fmt.Println(verdict(fmt.Errorf("west gate: %w", g.Admit("Ada", 23)))) fmt.Println(verdict(fmt.Errorf("after curfew, said the cook"))) fmt.Println(verdict(g.Admit("Ada", 9)))

expected.text: turned away, come back at dawn turned away admitted

testcode.text: g := NewGate([]string{"Ada", "Bram", "Cy"}, 22, 2) fmt.Println(verdict(g.Admit("Zed", 23))) fmt.Println(verdict(g.Admit("Zed", 9)), verdict(ErrHallFull)) fmt.Println(verdict(g.Admit("Ada", 10)), verdict(g.Admit("Bram", 10))) fmt.Println(verdict(g.Admit("Cy", 10)))

expected.text: turned away, fetch the steward turned away, fetch the steward turned away, wait by the fire admitted admitted turned away, wait by the fire
